idea-plugin.name: GPU Dev Accelerator Ultimate
idea-plugin.description:
GPU Dev Accelerator Ultimate — CUDA, Metal, and OpenCL Development

Write, compile, inspect, and analyze CUDA, Metal, and OpenCL code in a unified IDE environment. Every feature is backed by a real tool integration or deterministic analysis — no mock data.

GPU Language Support

  • Syntax highlighting for CUDA C/C++, Metal Shading Language, and OpenCL C (.cu, .cuh, .metal, .cl)
  • Code completion with API signatures for 100+ GPU builtins across all three languages
  • Quick documentation (Ctrl+Q) for kernel qualifiers, builtins, atomics, and warp primitives
  • Line/block commenting (Ctrl+/) and brace matching
  • Live templates: kernel skeletons, grid-stride loops, CUDA_CHECK macro, event timing, shared-memory tiles

Toolchain Integration

  • Compile CUDA files locally or through CLion's default remote SSH toolchain — errors clickable in the GPU Dev console
  • Show CUDA Assembly (PTX) beside its source with generated-line mapping
  • Memory checking via compute-sanitizer (or cuda-memcheck)
  • Kernel profiling via Nsight Compute (ncu) or nvprof
  • GPU inventory from nvidia-smi and system_profiler (Apple GPUs)
  • Live multi-GPU topology from nvidia-smi topo (NVLink/PIX/PHB/SYS links, utilization, memory)
  • Configurable toolchain paths, -arch, and extra nvcc flags in Settings | Tools | GPU Dev Accelerator

Static Analysis

  • Inspections: GPU memory leaks (cudaMalloc without cudaFree), unchecked CUDA API calls with a CUDA_CHECK quick fix, kernel performance heuristics
  • Kernel heuristics: strided access, warp divergence, __syncthreads() in divergent branches, missing bounds checks, missing __restrict__, device-side malloc, and more
  • Theoretical occupancy calculator for Volta through Hopper
  • Cross-platform kernel migration starting points (CUDA ⇄ Metal / OpenCL / HIP)

Requirements

  • Any IntelliJ-based IDE 2023.2 or newer
  • NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit for compile/profile/sanitize features
  • macOS for Apple GPU detection

Support

  • Documentation: GitHub Wiki
  • Community Forum: GitHub Discussions
  • Email: support@jakubjirak.com
  • Issues: GitHub Issues
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.9.1

  • Removed: The "Metal SDK (xcrun -sdk)" setting: the plugin never invokes xcrun or the Metal compiler, so the value had no effect. Metal support is editor-only (highlighting, completion, documentation, Migrate Kernel).

2026.9.0

  • Unchecked-CUDA-call inspection matches whole if/return keywords only.
  • Removed CUDA/Metal run configurations, the debug runner and breakpoint type that could not work.

2026.8.0

  • The plugin is now completely free — all features unlocked, no license needed.
  • Source code is now open source under Apache-2.0: https://github.com/JirakJ/gpu-dev-accelerator-ultimate

2026.5.0 — Production Overhaul

  • Real toolchain integration — nvcc compilation now runs in the background with clickable errors in the new GPU Dev console; no more UI freezes or modal dialogs
  • New: Show PTX — compile the current .cu file to PTX and inspect the generated code in the editor
  • New: Occupancy calculator — theoretical SM occupancy for Volta through Hopper with limiting-factor breakdown
  • New: Migrate Kernel action — CUDA ⇄ Metal/OpenCL/HIP source porting starting points
  • New: editor basics — Ctrl+/ commenting, brace matching, 8 live templates, quick documentation for 100+ GPU builtins
  • Real inspections — memory-leak and unchecked-API-call inspections now report problems in the editor; quick fix wraps calls in CUDA_CHECK
  • Real GPU data — GPU info, memory check (compute-sanitizer), profiling (Nsight Compute), and multi-GPU topology now read from the actual tools; simulated/placeholder outputs removed
  • New settings page — toolchain paths, GPU architecture, extra nvcc flags, timeouts

2026.4.1 — Critical Debug Runner Fix

  • Fixed: AbstractMethodError crash — Replaced deprecated GenericProgramRunner.doExecute() with ProgramRunner.execute() API compatible with IntelliJ 2024.3+
  • Fixed: Debug session hijacking — CudaDebugRunner.canRun() now only activates for CUDA/Metal run configurations
